target: Fais-moi penser à acheter du pain.
english: Remind me to buy bread.
tip: Faire + infinitive = make someone do something: fais-moi penser à acheter du pain is literally 'make me think to buy bread' – remind me to buy bread.

target: Certes, c'est difficile, mais pas impossible.
english: Certainly, it's difficult, but not impossible.
tip: Certes...mais: 'admittedly...but', concessive structure.

target: Je me suis fait voler mon téléphone.
english: I had my phone stolen.
tip: 'je me suis fait voler' isn't 'I made someone steal' – 'se faire' + infinitive marks something done TO you: I had my phone stolen.

target: Il m'a été impossible de la joindre.
english: It was impossible for me to reach her.
tip: 'il m'a été impossible' is literally 'it to-me was impossible' – that 'm'' names who couldn't do it: I couldn't reach her.

target: On m'a volé mon portefeuille dans le métro.
english: My wallet was stolen on the metro.
tip: French skips the passive for theft: on m'a volé mon portefeuille is literally 'they stole me my wallet.' The m' marks who got robbed, not who did it.

target: Ils allaient partir quand le téléphone a sonné.
english: They were about to leave when the phone rang.
tip: For 'about to,' French uses aller in the imperfect: ils allaient partir means 'they were about to leave' – not 'they used to leave.'

target: À moins que vous ne changiez d'avis, je procède.
english: Unless you change your mind, I'll proceed.
tip: That ne isn't a 'not': after à moins que, French drops in a decorative ne. Vous ne changiez d'avis still means 'you change your mind,' not 'you don't.'

target: Il ne viendra pas ; d'autant plus qu'il est malade.
english: He won't come, especially since he's sick.
tip: D'autant plus que: 'especially since/all the more because'.

target: Il n'a pas obtenu le poste ; toutefois, il ne perd pas espoir.
english: He didn't get the job; however, he's not losing hope.
tip: 'Toutefois' = however. Slightly more formal than 'cependant'. Used in written French.

target: Si bien que tout le monde était mécontent.
english: So much so that everyone was unhappy.
tip: Si bien que + indicative: 'so that/with the result that'.

target: Nous faisons repeindre l'appartement.
english: We're having the apartment repainted.
tip: Faire + infinitive: the subject causes the action but doesn't do it.

target: Aussi a-t-il décidé de partir.
english: Therefore, he decided to leave.
tip: At the start of a clause 'aussi' flips from 'also' to 'therefore' – and forces inversion: 'Aussi a-t-il décidé'. Put it mid-sentence and it's plain 'also' again.

target: Le bébé est en train de dormir.
english: The baby is sleeping.
tip: French has no '-ing'. To stress an action happening right now, use 'être en train de' + verb: 'est en train de dormir' = is in the middle of sleeping.

target: Il est trop speed en ce moment.
english: He's too wired right now.
tip: French slang borrows the English word 'speed' as an adjective meaning wired or hyper: 'il est trop speed' = he's too wound up. Nothing to do with velocity.

target: Nous venions de nous installer quand l'orage a éclaté.
english: We had just settled in when the storm broke out.
tip: Venir de in imparfait: 'had just done' in past context.

target: Le serveur nous a demandé ce que nous voulions boire.
english: The waiter asked us what we wanted to drink.
tip: In a reported question 'what' becomes 'ce que', never 'qu'est-ce que': 'nous a demandé ce que nous voulions' – no inversion, unlike a direct question.

target: Elle a demandé à ses enfants de ne pas faire de bruit.
english: She asked her children not to make noise.
tip: Negative reported command: de ne pas + infinitive.

target: Le médecin m'a conseillé de me reposer.
english: The doctor advised me to rest.
tip: 'conseiller' slips in a 'de' before the infinitive that English simply omits: 'conseillé de me reposer' = advised me to rest.

target: Bien qu'il soit fatigué, il continue de travailler.
english: Although he is tired, he keeps working.
tip: 'Bien que' + subjunctive: 'bien qu'il soit fatigué'. Concession always requires subjunctive in French.

target: Ma mère m'a demandé de ranger ma chambre.
english: My mother asked me to tidy my room.
tip: 'Demander de' + infinitive: reported imperative. 'Range ta chambre !' → 'elle m'a demandé de ranger'.

target: En dépit de ses efforts, elle n'a pas réussi.
english: Despite her efforts, she didn't succeed.
tip: 'En dépit de' = despite. More formal than 'malgré'. Both take a noun, not a clause.

target: Le projet est ambitieux ; en revanche, le budget est limité.
english: The project is ambitious; on the other hand, the budget is limited.
tip: 'En revanche' = on the other hand. Used for contrasting two facts. More formal than 'par contre'.

target: Force est de constater que nous avons échoué.
english: We are forced to admit that we have failed.
tip: Force est de + infinitive: formal 'one must acknowledge'.

target: L'avion est en train d'atterrir.
english: The plane is landing.
tip: French has no '-ing' tense. To pin an action to right now, wrap it in 'être en train de': 'est en train d'atterrir' = is in the middle of landing this very second.

target: Ils vont finir par accepter.
english: They'll end up accepting.
tip: 'Finir par' isn't about finishing – it means to end up doing something eventually: 'vont finir par accepter' = they'll come around to accepting in the end.

target: Il a filé à l'anglaise.
english: He left without saying goodbye.
tip: 'Filer à l'anglaise' = 'to slip away'. In English: 'French leave'.

target: Il a laissé tomber ses études.
english: He dropped his studies.
tip: 'Laisser tomber' is literally 'to let fall', but it means to drop or quit: 'a laissé tomber ses études' = gave up his studies. Also how you say you ditched someone.

target: Je viens de finir mon travail.
english: I just finished my work.
tip: 'Je viens de finir' means 'I just finished' – venir de + verb is French's recent past. It reads literally as 'I come from finishing', yet the plain present does past-tense work here.

target: Elle m'a demandé si j'avais faim.
english: She asked me if I was hungry.
tip: A reported yes/no question uses 'si' where a direct one used 'est-ce que': 'elle m'a demandé si j'avais faim' = she asked if I was hungry.

target: Je me suis fait couper les cheveux.
english: I got my hair cut.
tip: Se faire + infinitive: causative with reflexive, 'to get something done'.
